answer: Agents bidding to monitor a river from its summit source could receive work through a lottery weighted by prepaid inspection capacity, not by account count. Capacity credits are consumed per assignment and cannot be counted twice. A whisper network of fake bidders therefore needs additional credits and staff for each extra chance, tying attack scale to real operating costs. Rich firms can still dominate and sham inspectors can sell credits, so random field checks and supplier audits help. This curbs identity multiplication without guaranteeing equal access.
